outcomes.question: We incorporated a Singapore private company on 15 March 2026 and have one resident director. By when must we appoint a company secretary, and may the sole director fill that role?
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### ACRA — Corporate filing and governance

**Status:** Evidence verified

**ACRA company secretary appointment and sole-director requirements** (party in scope: Company)
- **ACRA rule explanation:** A company secretary must be appointed within six months of successful company registration, and the position cannot be vacant for more than six months. The secretary must be a natural person who meets the stated local-residency rules. The sole director cannot also act as the company secretary. The secretary is a required officer; check eligibility and residency independently of the appointment deadline. The single-director restriction applies where the only director would also be the secretary. ACRA’s page does not establish an extension or waiver of the appointment requirement. A case-specific conclusion requires: Successful registration date, current secretary, number of directors and which director is ordinarily resident. Candidate’s status as an individual and compliance with local residency eligibility. Current guidance; do not project this page onto an unverified historical incorporation period. A company-specific eligibility assessment requires the officer facts listed above.  The stated registration date reaches its six-month appointment deadline on 15/09/2026. [Step 4.3: Choosing company directors & other key officers | Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority](https://www.acra.gov.sg/register/business/registering-different-business-structures/local-company/appointing-company-directors-other-key-officers/)

**Source:** Step 4.3: Choosing company directors & other key officers | Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports ACRA company secretary appointment and sole-director requirements): A secretary must be appointed within six months of successful registration. The position cannot be empty for more than six months. Otherwise, the director may face a fine of up to $1,000.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports ACRA company secretary appointment and sole-director requirements): Note: Every company must have at least one company director and one company secretary.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports ACRA company secretary appointment and sole-director requirements): • Not be the same person as the sole director
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports ACRA company secretary appointment and sole-director requirements): • Be a real person (not a company)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports ACRA company secretary appointment and sole-director requirements): • Be a Singapore citizen, Singapore permanent resident, or someone who meets local residency rules

claims.text: A secretary must be appointed within six months of successful registration. The position cannot be empty for more than six months. Otherwise, the director may face a fine of up to $1,000.
Note: Every company must have at least one company director and one company secretary.
• Not be the same person as the sole director
• Be a real person (not a company)
• Be a Singapore citizen, Singapore permanent resident, or someone who meets local residency rules

outcomes.question: Our Singapore citizen employee earns total wages of S$400 in the month. Is there an employee CPF share, and must the employer still contribute?
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### CPF Board — CPF contributions

**Status:** Evidence verified

**CPF low-wage employer and employee contribution shares** (party in scope: Employer)
- **CPF rule explanation:** CPF Board selects the contribution table from citizenship or SPR year, age group and wage band. Total wages combine Ordinary Wages (OW) and Additional Wages (AW), which have separate ceilings. For wages above S$50 and up to S$500 in a month, the employee share is nil but the employer share remains due. Round the combined total contribution to the nearest dollar (50 cents rounds up); drop cents from the employee share and set the employer share to total less employee. To determine the actual amount, supply the payroll month, date of birth, status/PR conversion date, rate election, CPF-classified OW/AW, year-to-date contributions and expected annual OW where an AW ceiling applies. [CPF | How much CPF contributions to pay](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/how-much-cpf-contributions-to-pay)

Steps to compute CPF contribution:
1) Compute the total CPF contribution (rounded to the nearest dollar), i.e., to be rounded down for an amount less than 50 cents and rounded up for an amount of 50
cents and above.
2) Compute the employee’s share of CPF contribution (rounded down to the nearest dollar).
3) Employer’s share = Total contribution - Employee’s share
4) If there is only OW payable for the month, the maximum contribution on OW is to be rounded to the nearest dollar for the total CPF contributions and rounded down
to the nearest dollar for employee’s share of CPF contributions. If there are OW and AW payable for the same month, compute and sum up the CPF contributions
that are payable for OW and AW and apply the rounding rules accordingly.

to contribute to CPF at full employer- full employee rates.

Updates on 21 May 2026
To further strengthen the retirement adequacy of senior employees, there will be an increase to the CPF contribution rates from 1 Jan 2027. Find out more about these changes and how it affects you and your employees.
Current rates
What are the CPF contribution rates?
The following table summarises the current contribution rates for Singaporeans and SPRs (from third year and onwards) with monthly wages above $750, across the different age groups.
Employee’s age (years) | Contribution rates from 1 January 2026 (monthly wages > $750)
By employer (% of wage) | By employee (% of wage) | Total (% of wage)
55 and below | 17 | 20 | 37
Above 55 to 60 | 16 | 18 | 34
Above 60 to 65 | 12.5 | 12.5 | 25
Above 65 to 70 | 9 | 7.5 | 16.5
Above 70 | 7.5 | 5 | 12.5
View all tables (PDF, 0.2MB) for the full set of contribution rate tables covering all citizenship statuses and SPR years.
Computation
Determine your employees’ CPF contributions
CPF contribution rates vary based on your employee’s citizenship status, age group, and total wages. As an employer, you are required to pay CPF contributions for your employees who are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents and who are earning total wages of more than $50 per month.
Step 1: Select the contribution rate table based on citizenship status
Select the contribution rate table that applies to your employee.
Table 1: Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) from the third year of SPR status
Table 2: SPR in the first year of SPR status
Table 3: SPR in the second year of SPR status
Please ensure that your employees inform you the date when they became Singapore Citizens or SPRs, as different CPF contribution rates are applicable.
Determine the year of SPR status
The first year begins on the day of SPR conversion
The second year begins on the first day of the month after the first anniversary of SPR conversion
The third year begins on the first day of the month after the second anniversary of SPR conversion
Contribute more for first and second year SPRs
You and your employee who is in the first two years of SPR status can jointly apply to contribute CPF at a higher rate. The options are:
You and your employee both contribute at full rates (Table 1)
You contribute at full rates while your employee continues to contribute at graduated rates (Tables 4 and 5)
Step 2: Determine the rates based on age group and wage band
Different rates apply to different age groups.
New contribution rates apply from the first day of the month after the employee’s 55th, 60th, 65th or 70th birthday.
Different rates apply for different wage bands.
Step 3: Determine the Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
Apply the wage ceilings to determine Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
An employee’s CPF contributions are computed based on the Total Wages payable in a calendar month.
Total Wages are made up of an employee’s Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages. Different ceilings apply to Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages.
Step 4: Compute the CPF contributions on Total Wages
Compute Total CPF contributions
You can compute the total CPF contributions by applying the contribution rate to your employee’s total wages subject to CPF. The total CPF contributions comprise both your share as the employer and your employee’s share, which you are required to pay to the CPF Board. You are entitled to recover the employee’s share when paying your employee’s wages for the month.
Note that if your employee earns above $50 but not more than $500 per month, there is no employee’s share of CPF contributions. You will still need to pay the employer’s share.
Round off your Total CPF contributions
Please round off the Total CPF contributions to the nearest dollar. Cents should be dropped for amounts less than 50 cents, and amounts of 50 cents and above should be treated as an additional dollar. The cents should always be dropped for the employee’s share of CPF contributions.

Updates on 21 May 2026
To further strengthen the retirement adequacy of senior employees, there will be an increase to the CPF contribution rates from 1 Jan 2027. Find out more about these changes and how it affects you and your employees.
Current rates
What are the CPF contribution rates?
The following table summarises the current contribution rates for Singaporeans and SPRs (from third year and onwards) with monthly wages above $750, across the different age groups.
Employee’s age (years) | Contribution rates from 1 January 2026 (monthly wages > $750)
By employer (% of wage) | By employee (% of wage) | Total (% of wage)
55 and below | 17 | 20 | 37
Above 55 to 60 | 16 | 18 | 34
Above 60 to 65 | 12.5 | 12.5 | 25
Above 65 to 70 | 9 | 7.5 | 16.5
Above 70 | 7.5 | 5 | 12.5
View all tables (PDF, 0.2MB) for the full set of contribution rate tables covering all citizenship statuses and SPR years.
Computation
Determine your employees’ CPF contributions
CPF contribution rates vary based on your employee’s citizenship status, age group, and total wages. As an employer, you are required to pay CPF contributions for your employees who are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents and who are earning total wages of more than $50 per month.
Step 1: Select the contribution rate table based on citizenship status
Select the contribution rate table that applies to your employee.
Table 1: Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) from the third year of SPR status
Table 2: SPR in the first year of SPR status
Table 3: SPR in the second year of SPR status
Please ensure that your employees inform you the date when they became Singapore Citizens or SPRs, as different CPF contribution rates are applicable.
Determine the year of SPR status
The first year begins on the day of SPR conversion
The second year begins on the first day of the month after the first anniversary of SPR conversion
The third year begins on the first day of the month after the second anniversary of SPR conversion
Contribute more for first and second year SPRs
You and your employee who is in the first two years of SPR status can jointly apply to contribute CPF at a higher rate. The options are:
You and your employee both contribute at full rates (Table 1)
You contribute at full rates while your employee continues to contribute at graduated rates (Tables 4 and 5)
Step 2: Determine the rates based on age group and wage band
Different rates apply to different age groups.
New contribution rates apply from the first day of the month after the employee’s 55th, 60th, 65th or 70th birthday.
Different rates apply for different wage bands.
Step 3: Determine the Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
Apply the wage ceilings to determine Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
An employee’s CPF contributions are computed based on the Total Wages payable in a calendar month.
Total Wages are made up of an employee’s Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages. Different ceilings apply to Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages.
Step 4: Compute the CPF contributions on Total Wages
Compute Total CPF contributions
You can compute the total CPF contributions by applying the contribution rate to your employee’s total wages subject to CPF. The total CPF contributions comprise both your share as the employer and your employee’s share, which you are required to pay to the CPF Board. You are entitled to recover the employee’s share when paying your employee’s wages for the month.
Note that if your employee earns above $50 but not more than $500 per month, there is no employee’s share of CPF contributions. You will still need to pay the employer’s share.
Round off your Total CPF contributions
Please round off the Total CPF contributions to the nearest dollar. Cents should be dropped for amounts less than 50 cents, and amounts of 50 cents and above should be treated as an additional dollar. The cents should always be dropped for the employee’s share of CPF contributions.

Updates on 21 May 2026
To further strengthen the retirement adequacy of senior employees, there will be an increase to the CPF contribution rates from 1 Jan 2027. Find out more about these changes and how it affects you and your employees.
Current rates
What are the CPF contribution rates?
The following table summarises the current contribution rates for Singaporeans and SPRs (from third year and onwards) with monthly wages above $750, across the different age groups.
Employee’s age (years) | Contribution rates from 1 January 2026 (monthly wages > $750)
By employer (% of wage) | By employee (% of wage) | Total (% of wage)
55 and below | 17 | 20 | 37
Above 55 to 60 | 16 | 18 | 34
Above 60 to 65 | 12.5 | 12.5 | 25
Above 65 to 70 | 9 | 7.5 | 16.5
Above 70 | 7.5 | 5 | 12.5
View all tables (PDF, 0.2MB) for the full set of contribution rate tables covering all citizenship statuses and SPR years.
Computation
Determine your employees’ CPF contributions
CPF contribution rates vary based on your employee’s citizenship status, age group, and total wages. As an employer, you are required to pay CPF contributions for your employees who are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents and who are earning total wages of more than $50 per month.
Step 1: Select the contribution rate table based on citizenship status
Select the contribution rate table that applies to your employee.
Table 1: Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) from the third year of SPR status
Table 2: SPR in the first year of SPR status
Table 3: SPR in the second year of SPR status
Please ensure that your employees inform you the date when they became Singapore Citizens or SPRs, as different CPF contribution rates are applicable.
Determine the year of SPR status
The first year begins on the day of SPR conversion
The second year begins on the first day of the month after the first anniversary of SPR conversion
The third year begins on the first day of the month after the second anniversary of SPR conversion
Contribute more for first and second year SPRs
You and your employee who is in the first two years of SPR status can jointly apply to contribute CPF at a higher rate. The options are:
You and your employee both contribute at full rates (Table 1)
You contribute at full rates while your employee continues to contribute at graduated rates (Tables 4 and 5)
Step 2: Determine the rates based on age group and wage band
Different rates apply to different age groups.
New contribution rates apply from the first day of the month after the employee’s 55th, 60th, 65th or 70th birthday.
Different rates apply for different wage bands.
Step 3: Determine the Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
Apply the wage ceilings to determine Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
An employee’s CPF contributions are computed based on the Total Wages payable in a calendar month.
Total Wages are made up of an employee’s Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages. Different ceilings apply to Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages.
Step 4: Compute the CPF contributions on Total Wages
Compute Total CPF contributions
You can compute the total CPF contributions by applying the contribution rate to your employee’s total wages subject to CPF. The total CPF contributions comprise both your share as the employer and your employee’s share, which you are required to pay to the CPF Board. You are entitled to recover the employee’s share when paying your employee’s wages for the month.
Note that if your employee earns above $50 but not more than $500 per month, there is no employee’s share of CPF contributions. You will still need to pay the employer’s share.
Round off your Total CPF contributions
Please round off the Total CPF contributions to the nearest dollar. Cents should be dropped for amounts less than 50 cents, and amounts of 50 cents and above should be treated as an additional dollar. The cents should always be dropped for the employee’s share of CPF contributions.

Steps to compute CPF contribution:

Authority: CPF Board, Government of Singapore
Page title: How much CPF contributions to pay
Canonical official URL: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/how-much-cpf-contributions-to-pay
Capture date (Singapore): 2026-10-27
Capture method: verbatim visible text returned by a read-only browser extraction of the official HTML page. This is not a raw HTML response; exact excerpt text is retained below.

Updates on 21 May 2026
To further strengthen the retirement adequacy of senior employees, there will be an increase to the CPF contribution rates from 1 Jan 2027. Find out more about these changes and how it affects you and your employees.
Current rates
What are the CPF contribution rates?
The following table summarises the current contribution rates for Singaporeans and SPRs (from third year and onwards) with monthly wages above $750, across the different age groups.
Employee’s age (years) | Contribution rates from 1 January 2026 (monthly wages > $750)
By employer (% of wage) | By employee (% of wage) | Total (% of wage)
55 and below | 17 | 20 | 37
Above 55 to 60 | 16 | 18 | 34
Above 60 to 65 | 12.5 | 12.5 | 25
Above 65 to 70 | 9 | 7.5 | 16.5
Above 70 | 7.5 | 5 | 12.5
View all tables (PDF, 0.2MB) for the full set of contribution rate tables covering all citizenship statuses and SPR years.
Computation
Determine your employees’ CPF contributions
CPF contribution rates vary based on your employee’s citizenship status, age group, and total wages. As an employer, you are required to pay CPF contributions for your employees who are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents and who are earning total wages of more than $50 per month.
Step 1: Select the contribution rate table based on citizenship status
Select the contribution rate table that applies to your employee.
Table 1: Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) from the third year of SPR status
Table 2: SPR in the first year of SPR status
Table 3: SPR in the second year of SPR status
Please ensure that your employees inform you the date when they became Singapore Citizens or SPRs, as different CPF contribution rates are applicable.
Determine the year of SPR status
The first year begins on the day of SPR conversion
The second year begins on the first day of the month after the first anniversary of SPR conversion
The third year begins on the first day of the month after the second anniversary of SPR conversion
Contribute more for first and second year SPRs
You and your employee who is in the first two years of SPR status can jointly apply to contribute CPF at a higher rate. The options are:
You and your employee both contribute at full rates (Table 1)
You contribute at full rates while your employee continues to contribute at graduated rates (Tables 4 and 5)
Step 2: Determine the rates based on age group and wage band
Different rates apply to different age groups.
New contribution rates apply from the first day of the month after the employee’s 55th, 60th, 65th or 70th birthday.
Different rates apply for different wage bands.
Step 3: Determine the Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
Apply the wage ceilings to determine Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
An employee’s CPF contributions are computed based on the Total Wages payable in a calendar month.
Total Wages are made up of an employee’s Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages. Different ceilings apply to Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages.
Step 4: Compute the CPF contributions on Total Wages
Compute Total CPF contributions
You can compute the total CPF contributions by applying the contribution rate to your employee’s total wages subject to CPF. The total CPF contributions comprise both your share as the employer and your employee’s share, which you are required to pay to the CPF Board. You are entitled to recover the employee’s share when paying your employee’s wages for the month.
Note that if your employee earns above $50 but not more than $500 per month, there is no employee’s share of CPF contributions. You will still need to pay the employer’s share.
Round off your Total CPF contributions
Please round off the Total CPF contributions to the nearest dollar. Cents should be dropped for amounts less than 50 cents, and amounts of 50 cents and above should be treated as an additional dollar. The cents should always be dropped for the employee’s share of CPF contributions.

outcomes.question: For a Singapore citizen worker whose total monthly wages are S$250, does CPF require a deduction from the employee's wages as well as an employer contribution?
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### CPF Board — CPF contributions

**Status:** Evidence verified

**CPF low-wage employer and employee contribution shares** (party in scope: Employer)
- **CPF rule explanation:** CPF Board selects the contribution table from citizenship or SPR year, age group and wage band. Total wages combine Ordinary Wages (OW) and Additional Wages (AW), which have separate ceilings. For wages above S$50 and up to S$500 in a month, the employee share is nil but the employer share remains due. Round the combined total contribution to the nearest dollar (50 cents rounds up); drop cents from the employee share and set the employer share to total less employee. To determine the actual amount, supply the payroll month, date of birth, status/PR conversion date, rate election, CPF-classified OW/AW, year-to-date contributions and expected annual OW where an AW ceiling applies. [CPF | How much CPF contributions to pay](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/how-much-cpf-contributions-to-pay)

**Source:** CPF Contribution Rate Table from 1 January 2026 (live external)

Steps to compute CPF contribution:
1) Compute the total CPF contribution (rounded to the nearest dollar), i.e., to be rounded down for an amount less than 50 cents and rounded up for an amount of 50
cents and above.
2) Compute the employee’s share of CPF contribution (rounded down to the nearest dollar).
3) Employer’s share = Total contribution - Employee’s share
4) If there is only OW payable for the month, the maximum contribution on OW is to be rounded to the nearest dollar for the total CPF contributions and rounded down
to the nearest dollar for employee’s share of CPF contributions. If there are OW and AW payable for the same month, compute and sum up the CPF contributions
that are payable for OW and AW and apply the rounding rules accordingly.
5) To compute CPF contributions, use the CPF contribution calculator (cpf.gov.sg/employer > Tools and services > Calculators > CPF contribution calculator).

Notes:
For Private Sector / Non-Pensionable Employees (Ministries, Statutory Bodies & Aided Schools)
OW: Ordinary Wages (capped at OW ceiling of $8,000)
AW: Additional Wages
TW: Total Wages = OW + AW
Max: Maximum contribution on OW
Steps to compute CPF contribution:
1) Compute the total CPF contribution (rounded to the nearest dollar), i.e., to be rounded down for an amount less than 50 cents and rounded up for an amount of 50
cents and above.
2) Compute the employee’s share of CPF contribution (rounded down to the nearest dollar).
3) Employer’s share = Total contribution - Employee’s share
4) If there is only OW payable for the month, the maximum contribution on OW is to be rounded to the nearest dollar for the total CPF contributions and rounded down
to the nearest dollar for employee’s share of CPF contributions. If there are OW and AW payable for the same month, compute and sum up the CPF contributions
that are payable for OW and AW and apply the rounding rules accordingly.
5) To compute CPF contributions, use the CPF contribution calculator (cpf.gov.sg/employer > Tools and services > Calculators > CPF contribution calculator).

to contribute to CPF at full employer- full employee rates.

SOURCE CAPTURE METADATA
Authority: CPF Board, Government of Singapore
Page title: How much CPF contributions to pay
Canonical official URL: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/how-much-cpf-contributions-to-pay
Capture date (Singapore): 2026-10-27
Capture method: verbatim visible text returned by a read-only browser extraction of the official HTML page. This is not a raw HTML response; exact excerpt text is retained below.

Updates on 21 May 2026
To further strengthen the retirement adequacy of senior employees, there will be an increase to the CPF contribution rates from 1 Jan 2027. Find out more about these changes and how it affects you and your employees.
Current rates
What are the CPF contribution rates?
The following table summarises the current contribution rates for Singaporeans and SPRs (from third year and onwards) with monthly wages above $750, across the different age groups.
Employee’s age (years) | Contribution rates from 1 January 2026 (monthly wages > $750)
By employer (% of wage) | By employee (% of wage) | Total (% of wage)
55 and below | 17 | 20 | 37
Above 55 to 60 | 16 | 18 | 34
Above 60 to 65 | 12.5 | 12.5 | 25
Above 65 to 70 | 9 | 7.5 | 16.5
Above 70 | 7.5 | 5 | 12.5
View all tables (PDF, 0.2MB) for the full set of contribution rate tables covering all citizenship statuses and SPR years.
Computation
Determine your employees’ CPF contributions
CPF contribution rates vary based on your employee’s citizenship status, age group, and total wages. As an employer, you are required to pay CPF contributions for your employees who are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents and who are earning total wages of more than $50 per month.
Step 1: Select the contribution rate table based on citizenship status
Select the contribution rate table that applies to your employee.
Table 1: Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) from the third year of SPR status
Table 2: SPR in the first year of SPR status
Table 3: SPR in the second year of SPR status
Please ensure that your employees inform you the date when they became Singapore Citizens or SPRs, as different CPF contribution rates are applicable.
Determine the year of SPR status
The first year begins on the day of SPR conversion
The second year begins on the first day of the month after the first anniversary of SPR conversion
The third year begins on the first day of the month after the second anniversary of SPR conversion
Contribute more for first and second year SPRs
You and your employee who is in the first two years of SPR status can jointly apply to contribute CPF at a higher rate. The options are:
You and your employee both contribute at full rates (Table 1)
You contribute at full rates while your employee continues to contribute at graduated rates (Tables 4 and 5)
Step 2: Determine the rates based on age group and wage band
Different rates apply to different age groups.
New contribution rates apply from the first day of the month after the employee’s 55th, 60th, 65th or 70th birthday.
Different rates apply for different wage bands.
Step 3: Determine the Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
Apply the wage ceilings to determine Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
An employee’s CPF contributions are computed based on the Total Wages payable in a calendar month.
Total Wages are made up of an employee’s Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages. Different ceilings apply to Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages.
Step 4: Compute the CPF contributions on Total Wages
Compute Total CPF contributions
You can compute the total CPF contributions by applying the contribution rate to your employee’s total wages subject to CPF. The total CPF contributions comprise both your share as the employer and your employee’s share, which you are required to pay to the CPF Board. You are entitled to recover the employee’s share when paying your employee’s wages for the month.
Note that if your employee earns above $50 but not more than $500 per month, there is no employee’s share of CPF contributions. You will still need to pay the employer’s share.
Round off your Total CPF contributions
Please round off the Total CPF contributions to the nearest dollar. Cents should be dropped for amounts less than 50 cents, and amounts of 50 cents and above should be treated as an additional dollar. The cents should always be dropped for the employee’s share of CPF contributions.

Determine your employees’ CPF contributions

Step 1: Select the contribution rate table based on citizenship status
Select the contribution rate table that applies to your employee.

Table 2: SPR in the first year of SPR status
Table 3: SPR in the second year of SPR status

Determine the year of SPR status

The second year begins on the first day of the month after the first anniversary of SPR conversion
The third year begins on the first day of the month after the second anniversary of SPR conversion

You and your employee both contribute at full rates (Table 1)

outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

#### IRAS — GST

**Status:** Evidence verified

**GST input tax on staff medical expenses** (party in scope: Company)
- **IRAS rule explanation:** IRAS states that staff medical input tax is generally disallowed under regulation 26 of the GST (General) Regulations. Subject to the ordinary input-tax conditions, the stated exceptions are expenses obligatory under WICA or a qualifying Industrial Relations Act collective agreement; or, for expenses incurred on or after 1 October 2021, treatment connected with a work-related health risk or requirement and required under relevant Singapore written law. For the advisory limb, IRAS specifies treatment related to COVID-19 and required under a written advisory of the Government or a Singapore public authority. IRAS specifically says Primary Care Plan expenses do not meet the described work-related exception. A claim needs the expense date, legal/collective-agreement basis, work-related risk and mandate evidence, GST registration and invoice facts. [IRAS | Conditions for Claiming Input Tax](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-(gst)/claiming-gst-(input-tax)/conditions-for-claiming-input-tax)

**Source:** IRAS | Conditions for Claiming Input Tax (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports GST input tax on staff medical expenses): Input tax claims are disallowed under Regulation 26 of the GST (General) Regulations.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports GST input tax on staff medical expenses): However, subject to the conditions for input tax claim, these claims are allowed if: • the medical expenses (e.g. pre-employment and annual health screening expenses) are obligatory under the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA) or under any collective agreement under the Industrial Relations Act (IRA); or • the medical treatment in respect of expenses incurred on or after 1 Oct 2021 is provided in connection with any health risk or requirement due to the work nature or environment and mandated by written law or advisory.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports GST input tax on staff medical expenses): the medical treatment in respect of expenses incurred on or after 1 Oct 2021 is provided in connection with any health risk or requirement arising on account of the nature of the work required of your staff or his work environment; and ◦ the medical expenses are incurred pursuant to any written law of Singapore concerning the medical treatment or the provision of a medical facility or medical practitioner; or ◦ the medical treatment is related to COVID-19 and the staff undergoes such medical treatment pursuant to any written advisory (including industry circular) issued by, or posted on the website of, the Government or a public authority of Singapore.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports GST input tax on staff medical expenses): No, GST incurred on PCP will not be claimable. Based on the nature of the medical expenses covered under the PCP, the medical treatment is not provided in connection with any health risk or requirement arising on account of the nature of the work required of your staff or his work environment (e.g. employees exposed to radiation in the course of their work are required to undergo prescribed medical examinations by an approved medical practitioner). outcomes.question: Our VCFM opened a branch overseas. Does it need prior approval and what form is specified in the current MAS toolkit?
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### Monetary Authority of Singapore — Financial regulation

**Status:** Evidence verified

**MAS VCFM branch establishment prior approval and form** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** A VCFM must obtain MAS approval before establishing any branch in Singapore or elsewhere. Row 2 specifies no prescribed form and lists the matter under the MAS-Tx Entity Activities & Particulars category. This branch rule does not determine the row’s separate approval condition for acquiring or holding a 20% or greater interest in a corporation. Confirm that the manager is a VCFM and the proposed or completed activity is establishment of a branch. The approval is required before establishing the branch whether it is in Singapore or elsewhere. The toolkit row specifies no prescribed form; it identifies the MAS-Tx Entity Activities & Particulars category. The toolkit row does not establish the same branch-approval condition for an LFMC or another licence class. The branch approval rule does not answer the separate corporation-interest limb in row 2. The row requires prior approval but does not describe a retrospective approval or late-notification process. For case-specific application, consider: Confirm that the manager is a VCFM. Whether a branch is proposed or has already been established and its location. For a proposed branch, the expected establishment date; no date calculation is needed to state the prior-approval requirement. This rule is limited to the branch-establishment limb of row 2 and does not determine the separate 20% corporation-interest condition. The toolkit is not a complete statement of every VCFM obligation; this row does not describe an application package or post-establishment cure. [VENTURE CAPITAL FUND MANAGERS](https://www.mas.gov.sg/-/media/mas-media-library/regulation/guidance/cmi/compliance-toolkits-for-fund-management-companies/sfa-compliance-toolkit--vcfms29-may-2026-clean.pdf)

**Source:** VENTURE CAPITAL FUND MANAGERS (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports MAS VCFM branch establishment prior approval and form): 2 | To seek MAS’ approval to acquire or hold, whether directly or indirectly, an interest of 20% or more of the share capital of any corporation; or establish any branch (whether in Singapore or elsewhere). For this condition, "corporation" has the same meaning as in section 2 of the SFA, but excludes a corporation which is incorporated for the purpose of arranging a closed-end fund or a collective investment scheme | No prescribed form | Prior to the acquisition or control of a corporation, or the establishment of any branch | Licence condition or registration condition | MAS-Tx | Entity Activities & Particulars ( Establish/Acquire/ Hold Major Stake in a Corporation)
- Official source: [VENTURE CAPITAL FUND MANAGERS](https://www.mas.gov.sg/-/media/mas-media-library/regulation/guidance/cmi/compliance-toolkits-for-fund-management-companies/sfa-compliance-toolkit--vcfms29-may-2026-clean.pdf)
